visual: Compact clump-forming saxifrage with dark green scalloped leaves flushed purple and masses of delicate rose-pink flowers edged darker pink on slender stems.
water: Keep evenly moist during active growth, particularly in containers, but avoid stagnant wet conditions.
aspect: North, east or west-facing; partial to full shade.
soil: Humus-rich, moist but well-drained soil; tolerates acid, neutral and alkaline conditions.
soilWarning: Protect from hot, dry afternoon sun and prolonged winter waterlogging.
prune: Remove spent flower stems and damaged foliage after flowering.
resilience: Hardy through most of the UK where sheltered from excessive winter wet and drying exposure.
uses: Shady containers, woodland-style planting, rock gardens, border fronts and autumn colour.
uncertain: The earlier label fragment 'Dancing Pixies Twinkie' has been treated as an OCR duplicate of Dancing Pixies Toni because the later label explicitly states Toni.

visual: Fine-textured tufted ornamental grass with thread-like green foliage and clouds of arching silky pale green to buff flower panicles that move readily in wind.
water: Water while establishing; mature plants prefer moderately dry to evenly moist conditions.
aspect: South, east or west-facing; full sun.
soil: Moderately fertile, light to medium, well-drained soil of almost any pH.
soilWarning: Avoid persistently waterlogged ground and excessively rich soil that encourages floppy growth.
prune: Comb out dead foliage or cut back tired growth in early spring rather than autumn.
toxicity: Not generally considered poisonous, but fine leaves and awns may irritate skin, eyes or animals.
resilience: Tolerates drought, wind and exposed sunny positions once established.
uses: Gravel gardens, prairie planting, borders, containers, movement planting and architectural schemes.

visual: Compact Hybrid Tea rose with dark glossy foliage and large, shapely, high-centred, fully double velvety deep-red flowers opening from pointed buds.
water: Water deeply during dry weather, especially while establishing and when container-grown.
aspect: South, east or west-facing; full sun.
soil: Fertile, humus-rich, moist but well-drained soil of most textures and pH ranges.
soilWarning: Avoid waterlogging, severe drought and planting directly into soil recently occupied by another rose.
prune: Prune Hybrid Tea roses firmly in late winter or early spring, removing weak, damaged and crossing stems.
toxicity: Generally low toxicity; thorny stems can injure and ornamental fruits should not be treated as food.
resilience: Very cold hardy with relatively robust growth, though good airflow helps reduce common rose diseases.
uses: Rose beds, mixed borders, containers, fragrant gardens and cut flowers.

visual: Compact robust floribunda-style rose with glossy green leaves and clusters of slightly scented semi-double orange-red flowers repeating throughout summer and autumn.
water: Water deeply during prolonged dry periods and keep newly planted roses consistently moist.
aspect: South, east or west-facing; full sun.
soil: Fertile, humus-rich, moist but well-drained soil of most textures and pH levels.
soilWarning: Avoid waterlogged sites and exhausted rose-replant soil.
prune: Prune in late winter or early spring, reducing strong shoots and removing weak, damaged or crossing growth.
toxicity: Generally low toxicity; thorny stems can injure and ornamental fruits should not be eaten.
resilience: Cold hardy and repeat flowering, with routine rose care improving disease resistance and flowering.
uses: Borders, rose beds, containers, courtyard planting and cut flowers.

visual: Dense evergreen shrub or tree with glossy dark green, leathery, aromatic leaves and small yellow-green spring flowers; mature female plants may produce black berries.
water: Water moderately; established plants tolerate some drought but containers require regular watering.
aspect: South, east, west or sheltered north-facing; sun to partial shade.
soil: Moderately fertile, well-drained soil of almost any pH.
soilWarning: Avoid persistently wet ground and exposed frost pockets, especially for container-grown plants.
prune: Clip to shape in spring or summer; responds well to topiary and regular trimming.
toxicity: Leaves of true Laurus nobilis are culinary; berries are ornamental and should not be eaten.
resilience: Tolerates coastal conditions, pruning and short dry spells but container plants are more vulnerable to severe frost.
uses: Culinary herb, topiary, containers, hedging, evergreen structure and Mediterranean-style gardens.

visual: Small evergreen shrub with narrow glossy leaves and vivid bright-red young stems, petioles and new foliage, maturing green as the season progresses.
water: Keep evenly moist, particularly during establishment and in containers.
aspect: East, west or south-facing; sun to partial shade.
soil: Humus-rich, moist but well-drained acidic soil.
soilWarning: Requires acidic conditions; avoid lime, chalky soil and prolonged drought.
prune: Little pruning needed; remove old, damaged or poorly placed stems after flowering.
toxicity: Potentially harmful if eaten; Leucothoe foliage contains compounds associated with toxicity in the heath family.
resilience: Exceptionally cold hardy when grown in suitable acidic, moisture-retentive soil.
uses: Ericaceous containers, border fronts, woodland gardens, ground cover and colourful evergreen edging.

visual: Bushy upright English shrub rose with pink-tinged buds opening into clustered soft pale-yellow cupped flowers, fading creamy-white at the margins around a richer yellow centre.
water: Water deeply in dry weather, particularly through establishment and flowering.
aspect: South, east or west-facing; full sun, with some tolerance of partial shade.
soil: Fertile, humus-rich, moist but well-drained soil of most textures and pH levels.
soilWarning: Avoid waterlogged ground and badly depleted rose-replant soil.
prune: Prune as a repeat-flowering shrub rose in late winter, removing weak and congested stems and shortening remaining growth.
toxicity: Generally low toxicity; thorny stems can cause injury.
resilience: Cold hardy and repeat flowering; good airflow and routine rose care reduce common fungal problems.
uses: Mixed borders, rose borders, containers, low hedges, fragrant gardens and cut flowers.

visual: Compact mound-forming perennial with narrow green foliage covered by masses of dusky rose-pink daisy flowers in early and mid-autumn.
water: Keep moderately moist during active growth; water during prolonged summer drought.
aspect: South, east or west-facing; sun to partial shade.
soil: Fertile, moisture-retentive but well-drained soil of almost any pH.
soilWarning: Avoid prolonged waterlogging and extremely dry soil during flowering.
prune: Cut stems to ground level after flowering or in late autumn; divide congested clumps periodically.
resilience: Very cold hardy and relatively tolerant of exposed conditions.
uses: Autumn borders, wildlife gardens, containers, cottage gardens and pollinator planting.
uncertain: Rose Crystal is also encountered under the cultivar name Rose Quartz in the Autumn Jewels Series.

visual: Compact clump-forming Japanese anemone with dark green divided foliage and semi-double rose-pink flowers surrounding prominent golden-yellow centres in late summer and autumn.
water: Keep evenly moist during active growth, especially during prolonged dry periods.
aspect: East, west or south-facing; sun to partial shade.
soil: Humus-rich, fertile, moist but well-drained soil.
soilWarning: Avoid prolonged waterlogging and very dry exposed ground.
prune: Cut spent flowering stems back after flowering and remove old foliage as it dies back.
toxicity: Harmful if eaten; sap may irritate skin.
resilience: Cold hardy and reliable once established, performing best where roots remain reasonably cool and moist.
uses: Mixed borders, cottage gardens, woodland edges, containers and late-season pollinator planting.

visual: Compact dwarf cider gum with striking aromatic blue-green to silvery-blue juvenile leaves and a naturally bushier habit than the species.
water: Water regularly while establishing; established plants tolerate moderate dry periods.
aspect: South, east or west-facing; full sun.
soil: Moist but well-drained acidic to neutral loam, clay or sandy soil.
soilWarning: Avoid alkaline chalky soils, deep shade and stagnant winter water.
prune: Hard-prune or coppice in early spring if juvenile blue foliage and compact size are desired.
toxicity: Eucalyptus foliage and concentrated oils can be harmful if ingested in quantity, especially to pets.
resilience: Hardy in much of the UK when established and substantially more manageable than full-sized Eucalyptus gunnii.
uses: Architectural planting, blue foliage displays, containers, small gardens and cut foliage.
uncertain: The label fragment 'Bleu Eucalyptus Gunnii rance' has been interpreted as France Bleu.

visual: Compact evergreen heath shrub with small glossy dark green spine-tipped leaves, small pale flowers and decorative long-lasting pink to purplish berries.
water: Keep evenly moist, particularly during establishment and when grown in containers.
aspect: East, west or north-facing; partial shade to sun where soil remains moist.
soil: Humus-rich, moist but well-drained acidic soil.
soilWarning: Avoid alkaline or chalky soil and prolonged drought.
prune: Requires little pruning; remove dead, damaged or badly placed shoots in spring.
toxicity: Berries are ornamental and should not be eaten.
resilience: Hardy and evergreen when grown in suitably acidic soil with reliable moisture.
uses: Winter containers, ericaceous borders, woodland planting, ground cover and seasonal berry displays.
uncertain: 'Lilian' is a female cultivar and requires a compatible male plant nearby for reliable berry production.

visual: Strongly upright deciduous elder with deeply divided near-black purple foliage, forming a narrow architectural column and carrying flattened clusters of pink-flushed creamy flowers.
water: Water regularly while establishing; mature plants tolerate moderate periods of dryness.
aspect: South, east or west-facing; full sun to partial shade.
soil: Moderately fertile, moist but well-drained soil of most textures and pH ranges.
soilWarning: Best foliage colour develops in good light; avoid persistently waterlogged sites.
prune: Can be hard-pruned in early spring for vigorous foliage growth or lightly pruned to maintain its natural upright framework.
toxicity: Raw leaves, stems and unripe fruit contain compounds that can cause illness if eaten; ripe berries should be cooked before consumption.
resilience: Very hardy, vigorous and tolerant of a broad range of garden soils.
uses: Architectural borders, narrow spaces, wildlife gardens, dark-foliage schemes and informal screening.

visual: Evergreen climbing clematis producing nodding creamy bell-shaped winter flowers heavily spotted and freckled maroon-purple inside.
water: Keep roots moderately moist but well drained, particularly while establishing.
aspect: South or west-facing; sheltered sun or light partial shade.
soil: Fertile, humus-rich, moist but well-drained soil.
soilWarning: Avoid cold exposed positions, stagnant winter wet and severe frost pockets.
prune: Pruning group 1; generally requires no routine pruning beyond removing unwanted or damaged growth after flowering.
toxicity: Harmful if eaten; sap may irritate skin.
resilience: Hardy in sheltered UK gardens but winter foliage and flowers can be damaged by severe frost.
uses: Walls, fences, pergolas, winter-interest planting and sheltered courtyards.

visual: Compact evergreen shrub with glossy lance-shaped leaves emerging vivid red-purple before becoming green, then developing rich burgundy and scarlet tones in colder weather.
water: Keep consistently moist but never waterlogged.
aspect: East, west or north-facing; partial shade to filtered sun.
soil: Humus-rich, moisture-retentive but well-drained acidic soil.
soilWarning: Avoid alkaline soil, lime and prolonged drought.
prune: Little pruning required; remove damaged or congested shoots after flowering.
resilience: Very cold hardy provided roots remain moist and soil is suitably acidic.
uses: Ericaceous beds, woodland borders, containers, ground cover and winter foliage colour.

visual: Small evergreen shrub with unusually curled glossy leaves emerging red, becoming green and burgundy before developing rich red-purple winter colour.
water: Keep consistently moist, especially in containers and during establishment.
aspect: North, east or west-facing; partial shade.
soil: Humus-rich, acidic, moist but well-drained soil.
soilWarning: Avoid alkaline soil and drying out completely.
prune: Minimal pruning required; remove damaged or misplaced shoots after flowering.
resilience: Cold hardy and dependable in moist acidic conditions.
uses: Ericaceous containers, shady borders, ground cover, woodland gardens and winter foliage displays.

visual: Rounded deciduous shrub with glossy green leaves and unusual spherical creamy-white flower heads covered in projecting stamens, resembling tiny fibre-optic globes.
water: Prefers consistently moist to wet soil and tolerates seasonal waterlogging.
aspect: South, east or west-facing; full sun to partial shade.
soil: Moist to wet fertile soil with good organic content; adaptable to several soil textures and pH levels.
soilWarning: Avoid very dry sites where soil repeatedly dries out.
prune: Prune in late winter or early spring to shape or remove old and congested stems.
resilience: Very hardy and unusually tolerant of wet ground.
uses: Wildlife gardens, rain gardens, pond margins, wet borders and pollinator planting.

visual: Compact evergreen shrub with small glossy leaves splashed and margined in fresh lime-green, lemon-yellow and deeper green tones.
water: Water moderately and allow the surface to dry slightly between watering.
aspect: South or west-facing; full sun to light partial shade in a sheltered position.
soil: Fertile, well-drained soil or free-draining container compost.
soilWarning: Avoid waterlogging and exposed frost-prone positions.
prune: Trim lightly in spring to maintain a compact shape.
resilience: Wind and salt tolerant but vulnerable to hard inland frost.
uses: Containers, coastal gardens, colourful evergreen borders, patios and contemporary planting.

visual: Compact rounded deciduous shrub with small brilliant coral-red to burgundy leaves edged by a fine golden-yellow margin.
water: Water regularly while establishing; mature plants tolerate moderate drought.
aspect: South, east or west-facing; sun to partial shade.
soil: Well-drained soil of most textures and pH levels.
soilWarning: Best foliage colour develops in good light; avoid severe waterlogging.
prune: Little pruning required; trim after flowering or in late winter to maintain shape.
toxicity: Berries should not be treated as food; thorny stems may cause injury.
resilience: Extremely cold hardy, drought tolerant once established and adaptable to many soils.
uses: Low hedging, border fronts, containers, colour contrast and low-maintenance planting.

visual: Shrub or small tree with opposite leaves and clusters of flowers often followed by ornamental berries; exact appearance varies greatly between species and cultivar.
water: Most Viburnum prefer moderately moist soil, particularly during establishment.
aspect: Sun to partial shade depending on species.
soil: Generally fertile, humus-rich, moist but well-drained soil.
soilWarning: Exact soil and exposure requirements vary between Viburnum species.
prune: Pruning requirements depend on whether the plant flowers on old or new wood.
toxicity: Fruit toxicity and edibility vary between species; ornamental berries should not be eaten unless positively identified as edible.
resilience: Cannot be reliably scored beyond genus level.
uses: Borders, hedging, woodland planting, wildlife gardens and screening depending on species.
uncertain: Only 'Viburnum' was readable from the label. Species or cultivar is required for a reliable plant card.

visual: Compact evergreen shrub with small glossy dark green leaves and clusters of vivid rosy-red to crimson tubular flowers through summer.
water: Water regularly while establishing; mature plants tolerate modest dry periods.
aspect: South or west-facing; full sun in a sheltered position.
soil: Moderately fertile, well-drained soil of most textures and pH levels.
soilWarning: Avoid severe winter waterlogging and very cold exposed inland sites.
prune: Trim lightly after flowering to maintain a compact shape and remove frost-damaged shoots in spring.
resilience: Excellent coastal tolerance and good drought tolerance once established, though hard frost can damage foliage.
uses: Low hedging, coastal gardens, containers, sunny borders and pollinator planting.

visual: Upright panicle hydrangea producing large dense conical flower heads that open creamy white and rapidly develop pink, watermelon and rich reddish-pink tones as they mature.
water: Keep consistently moist during active growth, especially during hot weather and establishment.
aspect: South, east or west-facing; sun to partial shade.
soil: Fertile, humus-rich, moisture-retentive but well-drained soil.
soilWarning: Avoid very dry ground and prolonged waterlogging.
prune: Prune in late winter or early spring, shortening the previous season's shoots to a strong framework.
resilience: Very cold hardy and flowers reliably on new growth even after severe winters.
uses: Shrub borders, specimen planting, flowering hedges, large containers and cut or dried flowers.

visual: Compact evergreen camellia with glossy dark leaves and abundant semi-double to peony-form deep crimson-red flowers with conspicuous golden stamens in autumn and early winter.
water: Keep evenly moist, preferably using rainwater where tap water is strongly alkaline.
aspect: North, east or west-facing; sheltered partial shade or gentle sun.
soil: Humus-rich, moist but well-drained acidic soil.
soilWarning: Avoid alkaline soil, lime, prolonged drought and exposed positions where morning sun can rapidly thaw frozen flower buds.
prune: Usually requires little pruning; shape immediately after flowering if necessary.
resilience: Hardy in many UK gardens when sheltered, but flowers and buds are vulnerable to severe frost.
uses: Woodland gardens, sheltered borders, wall-side planting, containers and autumn flowering displays.

visual: Compact evergreen camellia with small glossy leaves and masses of delicate single blush-pink flowers surrounding golden stamens, often noticeably fragrant.
water: Keep evenly moist, using rainwater where possible in hard-water areas.
aspect: North, east or west-facing; sheltered partial shade.
soil: Humus-rich, moist but well-drained acidic soil.
soilWarning: Avoid alkaline conditions, lime, drought and exposed frost pockets.
prune: Requires little pruning; lightly shape after flowering if necessary.
resilience: Reasonably hardy in sheltered UK gardens, though flowers can be spoiled by hard frost.
uses: Fragrant gardens, containers, woodland borders, courtyards and sheltered wall-side planting.

visual: Low spreading evergreen to semi-evergreen perennial with glossy heavily scalloped near-black purple leaves and short spikes of intense blue-violet flowers.
water: Keep moderately moist, particularly during establishment and hot dry periods.
aspect: North, east, west or sheltered south-facing; sun to partial shade.
soil: Humus-rich, moist but well-drained soil of most textures and pH levels.
soilWarning: Avoid extremely dry ground and prolonged stagnant water.
prune: Trim spent flower spikes and remove unwanted runners to control spread.
resilience: Extremely cold hardy and tolerant of shade, with rapid ground-covering growth where moisture is adequate.
uses: Ground cover, border edging, containers, woodland planting, underplanting and pollinator gardens.

visual: Compact upright deciduous shrub with finely textured deep burgundy-purple foliage and rounded clusters of small pinkish-white flowers in early summer.
water: Water regularly while establishing; mature plants tolerate moderate drought.
aspect: South, east or west-facing; full sun to partial shade.
soil: Moderately fertile, moist but well-drained soil of most textures and pH ranges.
soilWarning: Deep shade reduces dark foliage colour; avoid severe waterlogging.
prune: Remove older stems after flowering or renovate gradually by cutting selected stems to the base.
resilience: Extremely cold hardy, adaptable and relatively tolerant of drought and urban conditions.
uses: Compact shrub borders, dark-foliage schemes, containers, low hedging and wildlife gardens.

visual: Dense upright deciduous shrub with rich reddish-purple new foliage maturing deep purple and clusters of pinkish-white flowers followed by decorative seed heads.
water: Water regularly during establishment; once established it tolerates moderate periods of drought.
aspect: South, east or west-facing; full sun to partial shade.
soil: Adaptable to most moderately fertile, moist but well-drained soils.
soilWarning: Best dark foliage colour develops in full sun; avoid persistent waterlogging.
prune: Prune after flowering if needed, removing older stems at ground level to maintain vigorous colourful growth.
resilience: Extremely cold hardy and highly adaptable to a broad range of garden conditions.
uses: Mixed shrub borders, screening, dark-foliage planting, wildlife gardens and informal hedging.
